geometryPolicy: 48 CSS pixel minimum action targets; project adaptations and unsupported variants documented in README

changes.description: Four common components that were missing: `bolle-bottom-app-bar` closes the Material 3 catalogue with a bottom container for actions, an end slot and an optional docked FAB, in a standard or floating form; `bolle-avatar`, `bolle-empty-state` and `bolle-pagination` are Schiuma primitives that the library itself was duplicating. The data table now renders `bolle-pagination` for its pager and `bolle-empty-state` for the empty and error rows, the kanban renders the same state for loading, error and empty, and the documentation demos drop their hand-written initials circle in favour of `bolle-avatar`. Component tokens `--md-comp-bottom-app-bar-*` and `--md-comp-avatar-*-size` added; pagination labels in English, Italian, French and Simplified Chinese.

`bolle-dashboard` takes the drag interaction promoted with `bolle-kanban`: dragging a tile by its handle now carries a copy that follows the pointer, opens a dashed gap in the slot the tile will occupy, names the position in the pointer note, refuses a drop outside the dashboard and scrolls the page or the nearest scroll container at the edges; Escape cancels with an announcement. Tile hover becomes a state layer on the surface, because the lift belongs to the moving copy, and Alt+arrows and the tile menu keep working as the path without dragging.

New Schiuma component `bolle-kanban` promoted from the approved prototype. The board renders columns and cards the application owns, moves them by pointer drag with a copy that follows the pointer, a dashed placeholder, a refused column in the error role and edge autoscroll, or by Alt+arrows from the card handle, and asks with `card-move` while `restrict` returns the reason a move is refused. Columns report the advised `wip` overrun without blocking, fold with `collapsed`, and carry the vertical scrolling so the board itself does not scroll; `lanes` stacks the cards in strips and `addable` offers a quick add. Card and column menus come from `cardActions` and `columnActions`, and the loading, error and empty states follow the table and shell contract.

New Schiuma components `bolle-app-shell` and `bolle-dashboard` with `bolle-widget`, promoted from the approved prototype. The shell lays out the bar, navigation, content, supporting pane, status and bottom bar as slots and picks the form from its own width, with `form` to force one and `form-change` to report it. The dashboard arranges twelve-column tiles that declare `span` and `min-span`, reorder them by drag, Alt+arrows or menu and resize them by handle, arrows or menu, reporting every change in `layout-change` and `widget-hide` while keeping the layout with the application.

Documentation site: App shell and Dashboard pages in the Schiuma section, with an interactive application preview that adapts to the stage width, a standalone dashboard preview that prints the layout it reports, controls for form, density, columns and supporting pane, and generated HTML, Vue and React snippets.

New Schiuma component `bolle-data-table`: a controlled table whose application owns rows, sorting, paging, grouping and selection and answers them through events. Columns carry width, alignment, pinning, grouping and a renderer; sorting keeps ranks and `aria-sort`; the header menu covers sorting, grouping, pinning, moving and hiding; columns drag with Escape and Alt+arrows; the resize handle works by pointer, double click and arrows. Selection, row details, group summaries, a pager, windowed rendering, loading/updating/empty/error states, `card` and `free` forms and two densities. Markup returned by renderers is styled through `contentStyles`.

Documentation site: Data table page in the Schiuma section with an interactive preview (sorting, grouping, paging, selection, details, column menu), controls, HTML/Vue/React snippets and the generated API table. The playground gives this entry the full width with the parameters underneath.

`bolle-menu` opens towards the wider side of the viewport on both axes: a menu under or over its anchor, a submenu beside its item, then clamps inside the viewport. Before, it opened below and in the reading direction and flipped only on overflow. Placement now reads the layout size of the surface: measuring during the entry animation read a scaled box, so the menu ran past its anchor and a submenu covered its parent.

`bolle-sidebar` gains `search`: `field` (default text field), `contained` or `divided` to filter with `bolle-search` in that appearance, `none` to hide the filter. The documentation site gives sidebar variants a column wide and tall enough to show the whole panel.

New Schiuma group for admin applications, outside the Material catalogue. First component `bolle-sidebar`: navigation tree up to three levels, filter, counters, ellipsis with a tooltip on cut labels, rail form with a menu beside it, resize grip (220–480px) and `edge`/`card` forms, built only on existing tokens.

Tail is optional: `tail="none"` on card, menu, tooltip, FAB menu and snackbar drops the narrow corner and keeps the same radius on all four corners. Documented in foundations, README and the component controls.

Token set cleanup: one declaration of `--md-sys-elevation-level2` (the second copy only repeated the value), and the two menu item shapes removed because item corners now derive from the container radius.
A link card shows one hover layer: the anchor inside the card no longer adds the shared link hover and glint on top of the card state layer.

Nested surfaces share one radius rule: an inner surface takes the container radius minus the padding the container applies, with a 2px floor. Dialogs, sheets and cards publish the value as `--bb-inset-radius` and a card placed inside them inherits it; the card tail is clamped to the card radius. Menu items, autocomplete and search suggestions derive their corners from the container radius, and docked date picker and time picker fields derive theirs from the calendar or dialog padding.

Built-in messages in French and Simplified Chinese besides English and Italian, chosen from the language subtag (`supportedLocale`); tab scroll buttons and the rich tooltip dismiss button are now localized instead of fixed English.

Tooltips wider than their trigger align their tail corner over the trigger centre (start-aligned, end-aligned near the right edge) instead of centring, and the tail side is computed from the final position rather than from the box scaled by the entry animation.
Slider `compact` attribute for the bubble variant: a 32px row with the value beside the label; the value bubble appears only while dragging or with keyboard focus.

Card `tail` property (`bottom-start` default, `bottom-end`, `top-start`, `top-end`) so the narrow corner points at where the card comes from. Link cards (`href`) make the whole surface the target, with a hover state layer, a raised float on elevated cards and a focus ring.

Scrollbars inside components have no arrow buttons and round track and thumb ends, inset from the container edges (`--bb-scrollbar-*`). Tabs with a fixed height keep the tab row in place and scroll only the panel.
List rows render the trailing count badge declared by the item `badge`, on the top-level rows and on the nested ones, with the badge tokens already used by tabs and the drawer.

Search bar geometry: the field wrapper grows with the bar, the input fills it, the label and supporting text stay only in the accessibility tree and the focus indicator is drawn on the bar instead of a smaller box inside it.
Connected button group inner corners follow the M3 per-size values (XS 4dp, S/M 8dp, L 16dp, XL 20dp) with the hovered growth specified for each size, instead of reusing the shape scale.
Select and autocomplete components over native options; per-component spacing tokens with Material names for navigation rail, list, carousel and search bar; field height and vertical padding tokens.
35 component entries, public types, shared action/form/surface tokens and catalogue examples; existing menu and generated typography retained.
